headline: High: shared filesystem plus broad plugin/MCP egress creates prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risk in the Copilot–Semantic Kernel pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open buffers and can propose edits; Semantic Kernel can use MCP/OpenAPI tools and broad egress. If SK ingests Copilot-authored content from shared files or buffers, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream tool use. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel reads Copilot-generated file content or buffers as instructions
IF an MCP/OpenAPI plugin executes prompts derived from that content
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Copilot-authored files into SK prompts
Add a provenance tag to all Copilot outputs before SK consumes them
Require human review before any SK tool call triggered by repo text
Restrict SK plugins to allowlisted endpoints only
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers, while Semantic Kernel handles application context and secrets such as model provider API keys and plugin credentials. If they share a workspace or memory store, sensitive code or secrets can flow from one agent into the other’s prompts or outputs. The profiles do not show isolation strong enough to rule this out.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace, repo, or memory store
IF SK forwards file contents or context into a third-party model/API
mitigations: Separate Copilot and SK workspaces immediately
Remove secrets from any shared context before SK runs
Turn off automatic file-content upload where possible
Use distinct credentials for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention and redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state; Semantic Kernel can also write the filesystem and invoke plugins/MCP tools. In a shared directory or repo, concurrent writes can overwrite each other or corrupt git state. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive between them, so conflict is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF SK plugins or Copilot Workspace apply edits concurrently
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout or directory
Pause one agent before the other writes
Require git status checks before every write
Avoid concurrent plugin actions on shared files
requires-engineering: add file-level locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces code edits and chat suggestions, and Semantic Kernel is a multi-agent orchestration layer that can treat upstream outputs as inputs to plugins or agents. If SK accepts Copilot output without verification, incorrect code or fabricated facts can cascade into automated actions or further generated artifacts. That default pathway is dangerous because the downstream agent can operationalize the error.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel consumes Copilot output without a verification step
IF SK uses that output to call plugins, APIs, or generate further agent prompts
mitigations: Insert a verification step before SK uses Copilot output
Require citations or tests for any code suggestion before execution
Limit SK to read-only analysis of Copilot output
Log and review all downstream tool calls
requires-engineering: implement structured validation between the agents

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is tied to GitHub repo context and editor buffers, while Semantic Kernel explicitly handles model-provider API keys and plugin credentials and can send data to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or MCP servers. If regulated data enters both systems, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the mismatch risk is material.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared repo or application context
IF SK forwards that data to a provider with different retention or residency terms
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared prompts and repos
Use provider settings that minimize retention
Review vendor DPAs before enabling both agents on sensitive data
Separate EU and US workloads by workspace
requires-engineering: enforce residency-aware routing and retention controls
